newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MARADONA SHOW BACK IN TOWN AS BOCA WIN 3-2.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARADONA SHOW BACK IN TOWN AS BOCA WIN 3-2.

text.p: Argentina's ageing idol Diego Maradona returned to bask once more in his own legend Sunday, officially making his fifth comeback to soccer before worshipping Boca Juniors fans and leading his team to a 3-2 victory over Racing Club.

The Boca Juniors stadium in the rough port district of Buenos Aires was packed with supporters anxious to see a great player whose every game threatens to be his last, at least until his next comeback.

Maradona did not put in a great performance, which these days is hardly expected of him, but he fired up the troubled Boca Juniors team, stuck in the middle of the Argentine first division table with the season nearly over, and gave the public nearly an hour of his exulted presence.
Today's venerable Maradona does not deign to run after the ball much, but the other players dutifully passed to him as much as possible and his touch in the set-pieces was masterful.

A wicked, curling ball from a free-kick outside the area on right field two-thirds into the first half was just deflected by Racing's Argentine national team goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez. Minutes later, Maradona booted a similar free-kick from left field, plopping the ball just in front of Nestor Fabbri, who headed it down and into the goal to put Boca up 3-1.

It was Maradona's first official league game for almost a year. His short-frame, which usually shows plain evidence of a well-known liking for pizza, is 24 pounds (11 kg) lighter thanks to a tough fitness programme in Canada under the supervision of sprinter Ben Johnson.

Johnson, like Maradona, shares the shame of a drug ban from sport. An earlier Maradona comeback was foiled in a humiliating fashion when he was expelled from the 1994 World Cup Finals in the United States after his urine tested positive for a stimulant.

The hero of Argentina's 1986 World Cup triumph has since struggled with a confessed cocaine problem, and his last comeback with Boca petered out as he gradually stopped bothering to show up for matches last year.
This time round, Maradona says he is serious. He will not play the remaining three fixtures this season to concentrate on getting ready for the new season which starts on August 24.

All past sins were forgiven Sunday night. The other Boca players, generally little more organised on the pitch than Maradona's social life, charged around with the conviction that the force was with them.

But Maradona's distinctive bow-legged gait became more exaggerated as the match wore on and he slowed down, particularly after being fouled hard in the shin late in the first half. Eventually it was too much for his 36-year-old frame, and Maradona charged off the field to an ovation 10 minutes into the second half, crossed himself, got a kiss from grateful trainer Hector Veira, and that was all, folks.
